answer: Mature ecosystems all offer some private-mirror, federation, and offline story, but they do not share one index shape. Designs whose *index unit* is already one JSON object (conda repodata.json per subdir, Nix flake-registry.json, a static gallery JSON) survive a git-file index: clone the file, resolve packages, fetch blobs separately. Designs whose index is a sharded git tree (Cargo), a dists/pool metadata tree (apt), a CouchDB/live HTTP registry (npm), a GOPROXY URL tree, or a per-project simple index (PEP 503/691) do not survive the single-JSON constraint even when they already use git or already support offline install. Control negative: Cargo's git index is git, and still fails.

claims.claim: A conda-style channel index whose lookup unit is one JSON file (repodata.json) survives a git-file index: git can version that file and a client can resolve packages by reading it.

conda-build docs: each subdir has its own repodata.json

claims.strongest_caveat: Production conda channels emit one repodata.json per platform subdir (linux-64, noarch, ...), not one global file. Survival is at the subdir-file grain. Blobs remain beside the JSON.

claims.canonical_mechanism: single flake-registry.json name-to-URI map in git
claims.claim: The Nix flake registry design survives a git-file index because the default registry is one JSON file in a git repository.

claims.strongest_caveat: The registry maps names to flake URIs; it is not a package-blob index. Offline install still needs the nix store / fetched flakes.

claims.claim: A static marketplace catalog encoded as one JSON file plus content-addressed blobs survives a git-file index. Federation that requires a live uplink does not; merge-in-git does.

claims.strongest_caveat: Homebrew's public formula JSON is a generated API view; Homebrew taps themselves are git trees of Ruby files (see C9). The surviving design is the JSON-catalog shape, not brew tap as shipped.

claims.canonical_mechanism: git index with config.json plus one file per crate
claims.claim: Cargo's git registry index does not survive a single-JSON git-file index: the catalog is a sharded per-crate file tree.

source_lineage.note: crates.io-index config.json is only dl+api URLs, not the catalog
Cargo book: one file for each package in a sharded tree

claims.strongest_caveat: Cargo still supports offline via vendor/local-registry, and private registries via a git URL. Those features survive; the *single JSON file* constraint does not.

claims.claim: Debian apt repository metadata does not survive a git-file index: clients fetch a Release file that enumerates many Packages files.

claims.strongest_caveat: You can store an apt mirror in git, but the index shape is still a multi-file dists tree, not one JSON file.

claims.canonical_mechanism: CouchDB document replication or live HTTP proxy
claims.claim: npm's mature private-mirror designs (CouchDB replicate, Verdaccio uplink) do not survive a git-file index because the replication unit is a document database or a live registry API.

source_lineage.note: GitHub API: Verdaccio is a private proxy registry, not a git JSON catalog
npm docs: public registry powered by CouchDB; public mirror skimdb

claims.strongest_caveat: A frozen npm pack tarball set plus a handmade catalog JSON would be the static-gallery design (C3), not npm's published mirror protocol.

claims.claim: The Go module proxy protocol does not survive a git-file index: lookup is a per-module URL tree, not one JSON catalog.

claims.strongest_caveat: go mod vendor produces a directory of module sources; that is an offline export, not a federated registry index encoded as one JSON file.

claims.canonical_mechanism: PEP 503 simple index: one page per project
claims.claim: PEP 503/691 simple indexes do not survive a single-JSON git-file index: each project is its own document.

design_table.design: Conda channel with per-subdir repodata.json plus package blobs
design_table.federated_index: client lists multiple channels; each channel is its own index
design_table.offline: local channel directory; conda install --offline after cache fill
design_table.private_mirror: copy the channel directory or serve file:// / HTTPS of the same tree
design_table.why: The lookup unit is already one JSON object (repodata.json) mapping filenames to metadata. Git can version that file; a client reads it without a query API. Caveat: production channels use one JSON per platform subdir, not one global file.

design_table.design: Nix flake registry: one JSON file mapping short names to flake URIs, hosted in git
design_table.federated_index: additional registries can be configured; the default is one file
design_table.offline: already-fetched nix store paths; the registry JSON still only names URIs
design_table.private_mirror: point nix at a forked registry JSON (flake-registry.json in a git repo)
design_table.why: The published default registry is literally one flake-registry.json in a git repository. That is the git-file-index shape.

design_table.design: Static marketplace/plugin gallery as one catalog JSON committed to git plus content-addressed blobs
design_table.federated_index: federation-by-merge (combine catalogs in git). Live uplink proxies do not survive.
design_table.offline: clone + blob store; install from recorded blob ids
design_table.private_mirror: git clone of the catalog repo; serve or read the JSON locally
design_table.why: A catalog whose schema is {packages:[{id,version,blob}]} is exactly one JSON git blob. Local fixture git-file-ok/marketplace.json demonstrates lookup.

design_table.design: Cargo registry git index (crates.io-index): config.json plus one file per crate
design_table.failing_property: path-sharded per-crate index files; collapsing them breaks cargo's index layout
design_table.federated_index: [registries] extra git or sparse+ URLs in .cargo/config.toml
design_table.layout_failing_property: index is a path-sharded tree of per-crate files plus config.json, not one JSON catalog
design_table.offline: cargo vendor / [source.crates-io] replace with directory or local-registry
design_table.private_mirror: git clone of the index plus a crate download mirror; or sparse+ HTTP of the same tree
design_table.why: Cargo's git protocol is an index in git, but the index is a sharded tree: one file per package, not one JSON file.

design_table.design: Debian apt repository: dists/pool with InRelease/Release and Packages indices
design_table.failing_property: dists/*/Release + per-component Packages files; not a single JSON catalog
design_table.layout_failing_property: index is dists/*/Release plus per-component Packages files, not one JSON file
design_table.offline: local mirror or apt-offline; packages retrieved from pool/
design_table.private_mirror: debmirror / aptly / reprepro of the dists+pool tree
design_table.why: The index is a signed multi-file dists tree (Release lists many Packages files). It is not JSON and not one file.

design_table.design: npm registry CouchDB replication or a live proxy (Verdaccio uplink)
design_table.failing_property: document database / live registry API is the replication unit, not one git JSON file
design_table.federated_index: Verdaccio uplinks chain registries into one endpoint
design_table.layout_failing_property: replication unit is a document database (_changes + per-id docs), not one git JSON catalog
design_table.offline: Verdaccio disk cache / npm pack / local file: tarballs
design_table.private_mirror: historical: replicate skimdb; current: Verdaccio/uplink proxy cache
design_table.why: The public registry is a CouchDB; clients talk HTTP JSON per package. Replication is a document _changes feed, not a git JSON file.

design_table.design: Go module proxy (GOPROXY) plus checksum database
design_table.failing_property: per-module URL tree + optional sumdb; not a single JSON git blob
design_table.federated_index: GOPROXY is a comma-separated URL list
design_table.layout_failing_property: index is a path-sharded tree of per-crate files plus config.json, not one JSON catalog
design_table.offline: vendor/ directory or GOPROXY=off with a filled module cache
design_table.private_mirror: Athens / goproxy binary serving the module path tree
design_table.why: The proxy protocol is a URL-addressed tree (list, info, zip, mod per module version), not one JSON catalog.

design_table.design: PEP 503 HTML simple repository, optionally PEP 691 per-project JSON
design_table.failing_property: per-project simple documents (HTML or PEP 691 JSON), not one git JSON catalog
design_table.layout_failing_property: index is dists/*/Release plus per-component Packages files, not one JSON file
design_table.offline: pip download + --no-index --find-links; or a local simple tree
design_table.why: The simple API is a page (HTML or JSON) per project under /simple/<name>/, plus a root project list. That is N documents, not one catalog JSON.

evidence_tier_ledger.E1: verbatim extract from a canonical spec plus a second independent structured observation of the same mechanism (not claimed here)
evidence_tier_ledger.E2: two mechanically independent rails (structured HTTP API/schema/JSON and a prose spec/doc), each with permalink, fetch timestamp, HTTP 200, and sha256 of captured bytes
evidence_tier_ledger.E3: single rail only; may not be cited as measured fact; adversarial default REFUTED
evidence_tier_ledger.E4: degraded fetch or inferred mechanism (needle missing from captured bytes)

git_file_index_rule: survives-git-file-index means a client can resolve every catalogued package id+version to a blob locator by reading one JSON file retrieved as a git blob (clone or sparse-checkout of that path). No live query API, document database, or generated multi-file metadata tree is required for index lookup. Blobs may sit beside the JSON; they are not the index.
question: How do mature ecosystems support private mirrors, federated indexes and fully offline install/export - and which of those designs works when the index is a single JSON file in a git repository?

reviewer.notes: Default REFUTED unless a claim carries structured-api + prose rails with live sha256 match. C10 (single rail) stays REFUTED. Overclaim 'cargo git index is one JSON file' is REFUTED.

overclaim_control.overclaim: The Cargo git registry index is a single JSON file and therefore survives a git-file index.
overclaim_control.reason: Cargo book: the index repository contains one file for each package, sharded by name. Fixture cargo-sharded has config.json plus per-crate files.
